text:
maria_su: FYI support ticket #4521 — ACME reported a negative ledger after a chargeback + promo reversal. Trial credits disappeared and final balance shows -$120. Link to billing event: https://billing.internal/acme/events/98765

maria_su: customer id: acct_9z7, invoice 2026-03-10-ACME, chargeback event recorded at 1772499900. I grabbed the raw event stream — looks like promo revoke happened twice.

devon_k: Can you paste the event IDs + webhook payloads? Need to see if the grant was removed twice or an invoice adjustment duplicated.

maria_su: here are the two webhook deliveries (sanitized):
```
{ "event": "promo_revoked", "grant_id": "g-321", "reason": "chargeback", "delivery_id": "d-9001", "attempt": 1 }
{ "event": "promo_revoked", "grant_id": "g-321", "reason": "chargeback", "delivery_id": "d-9002", "attempt": 2 }
```

maria_su: ops-bot shows second delivery as a retry because downstream handler returned 5xx at 1772501400.

samir_eng: This smells like a webhook idempotency gap. The grant removal should be idempotent on grant_id. Looking at processor logs — it processed both deliveries and created two negative adjustments: adj_555 and adj_556.

samir_eng: quick log snippet:
```
[1772501401] process_webhook d-9001 -> revoke grant g-321 -> created adjustment adj_555 (-$60)
[1772501405] downstream 500 error -> retry queued
[1772501499] process_webhook d-9002 -> revoke grant g-321 -> created adjustment adj_556 (-$60)
```

devon_k: So customer had $60 of trial credits and we removed them twice -> -$120. Was there also a chargeback refund that subtracted another $X? Need combined effect on invoice.

maria_su: Chargeback reversed the original payment of $200, then the two promo revocations removed $60 twice; net ledger = -$120 (customer now owes us). Customer expects zero or refunded — they are upset.

lena_pm: What are the immediate customer-facing actions? We should stop automated collections and open a support refund hold.

devon_k: Agreed — put invoice 2026-03-10-ACME on hold and mark for manual review. I'll create a manual credit memo to correct and issue a refund if policy allows.

samir_eng: Engineering plan: make webhook processor idempotent by storing processed (grant_id, event_type) keys and rejecting duplicates. Also patch downstream to return 200 if adjustment already exists. Quick mitigation: run a one-off audit to merge duplicate adjustments where grant_id==g-321 and created within same 10m window.

maria_su: Repro steps for SRE/QA to validate patch:
1) create a test account with a promo grant g-test-1 ($10).
2) send promo_revoked webhook d-a (attempt 1) -> expect one adjustment created.
3) simulate downstream 500 then send d-b (retry) -> expect no second adjustment.

samir_eng: I'll put a fix in a hotfix branch and deploy to staging. Tagging @ops-bot for rollout: ops-bot, please coordinate canary to staging then prod.

ops-bot: Deployment scheduled: hotfix/webhook-idempotency -> staging at 2026-03-17T15:30Z, canary to prod pending QA signoff. :gear:
devon_k: I'll handle the billing correction and customer note. Maria, can you confirm ACME wants a refund vs. credit?

maria_su: ACME prefers a refund to original payment instrument. I've requested bank details and asked for patience.

lena_pm: Action items summary:
- devon_k: hold invoice & create credit memo / refund (P0)
- samir_eng: idempotency hotfix + audit script (P0)
- maria_su: confirm customer refund details & update ticket (P0)
- ops-bot: coordinate rollout (awaiting QA)

maria_su: tagging this thread for postmortem once resolved. We'll need an internal note for billing ops and a short KB for how promo revokes interact with chargebacks. :memo:
